text: The LORD reigns; let the peoples tremble. He is enthroned on the cherubim; let the earth shake.

versions.text: The LORD reigns; let the nations tremble. He is enthroned on the cherubim; let the earth quake.
versions.explanation: עַמִּים is more precisely 'peoples' (as distinct from גּוֹיִם, 'nations'); 'shake' also pairs more naturally with 'tremble' for oral reading. Minor refinement only.

text: Great is the LORD in Zion; he is exalted above all the nations.
Let them praise your great and awesome name—he is holy.
The King is mighty, and he loves justice. You have established fairness; you have brought about justice and righteousness in Jacob.

versions.text: Mighty king, lover of justice, you have established what is right; you have brought about justice and righteousness in Jacob.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew clause is a third-person statement ('the strength of the King loves justice') before shifting to direct address. The vocative 'Mighty king, lover of justice' both changes the person and reads a little stiff aloud; a short declarative sentence followed by the address preserves the Hebrew's movement and flows better.

text: Exalt the LORD our God; bow down before his footstool—he is holy.
Moses and Aaron were among his priests, and Samuel among those who called on his name; they called on the LORD, and he answered them.
He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud; they kept his testimonies and the statute he gave them.
LORD our God, you answered them. You were a forgiving God to them, yet you punished their misdeeds.
Exalt the LORD our God; bow down at his holy mountain, for the LORD our God is holy.
